Game: Move a point around a half-circle and watch three lines; there is nothing to win or lose.
How to play: Drag O or X, or focus one and press the arrow keys. Tick the boxes to show the point names or the matching-length marks.

Drag O or X, or focus one and press the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps).

Look for the math

This is a droodle from Five Hundred Mathematical Challenges: move X and the three coloured lines either all meet in one place, or none of them do. The same thing happens at every position on the circle — the logic test checked 4,000-plus pictures, from X almost at A all the way round to X almost at B.

The claim, and one slip on the old page

Let AB be the diameter, O its centre, and X any other point on the arc. The tangents at A, X and B are drawn. The line BX meets the tangent at A at Y, and AX meets the tangent at B at Z. The old page claims that the tangent at X, the line YZ and the line AB are concurrent or else all parallel. The logic test confirms this for every sampled position. One line of the old proof says "V is the midpoint of BV"; it must mean BZ — V lies on the tangent at B. The old applet also always drew the lower half of the circle although it put X above AB; here the arc follows X, as the page's "semicircle AXB" says.

Why U and V are midpoints

Let U be where the tangent at X meets the tangent at A. The two tangents from U touch the same circle, so UA = UX. Because AB is a diameter, angle AXY is a right angle, and AY's midpoint is equally far from A, X and Y: it must be U. Hence UA = UX = UY. The same argument at B gives VB = VX = VZ, so V is the midpoint of BZ. Tick Show hint to see the matching slashes on those three lengths at U.

Where the three lines meet

Write the radius as r and put X at angle t above AB, so its offset from O is (r cos t, r sin t). The midpoint facts give the coordinates U = (-r, r cot(t/2)) and V = (r, r tan(t/2)), measured from O with up positive. Chasing the line YZ through the two midpoints gives the meeting point P = (r / cos t, 0), which lies on AB extended. The tangent at X has equation x cos t + y sin t = r, and P satisfies it too: (r / cos t) · cos t + 0 = r. When cos t = 0 — X at the top of the arc — P runs off to infinity and the three lines are parallel instead.

Drag X towards the top of the arc and watch the meeting point travel further and further out along AB, then disappear when the lines become parallel.

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
